The median home in Palos Hills was built in 1977. Across the 7,885 housing units here, 63.3 percent went up before 1980 and 0.2 percent date to 1939 or earlier. That single figure decides more about a paint job than anything else anyone will ask you on the phone.

Palos Hills is 79.6 percent owner occupied, 5,831 households against 1,496 renting. 45.8 percent of units are in buildings of two or more, 11.8 percent are attached, and the remaining 42.4 percent are detached houses averaging 5.3 rooms. Median value across that stock is $259,200.

Where Palos Hills departs most from the 76 place average: prewar housing at 0.2 percent against a 15.8 percent average, housing built before 1970 at 19.8 percent against a 56.9 percent average and housing in buildings of two or more at 45.8 percent against a 29 percent average.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

What that means for a paint job in Palos Hills

On a 1977 house the wall area outside is usually small and the detail is not. Fascia, soffit, the garage door surround, the front entry and the window trim is a narrow band of work that adds up, and it is exactly what gets underestimated by anyone quoting off photographs instead of standing there. 45.8 percent of the housing sits in buildings of two units or more, which means hallways, stairwells and unit turnarounds are as much of the work as living rooms. Those get quoted per unit and they get done to a date.

The lines a quote for Palos Hills needs to show

  • Per unit, to a date. 45.8 percent of units here are in buildings of two or more. Turnover work is priced per unit and scheduled to a move-out, not to the weather.
  • Matching, exactly. 11.8 percent of units are attached, and on a shared elevation close is not good enough. Existing color has to be matched rather than approximated.
  • Distance, stated. Palos Hills is 2.9 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Palos Hills is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 63.3 percent of housing in Palos Hills was built before 1980, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is 1970s stock with a large share of townhomes and apartment units. Association work, matching an existing scheme exactly and painting several identical units in a row, is as much of the Palos Hills market as single-house work.

That reading comes from two numbers on this page and nothing else: a median build year of 1977 and a structure split of 42.4 percent detached, 11.8 percent attached and 45.8 percent in buildings of two or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in Palos Hills is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

Palos Hills is mostly pre-1978 stock, and that changes the setup

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 63.3 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Palos Hills. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

Read it as a method rather than a prohibition. Below roughly six square feet of disturbed paint in a room, or twenty outside, it does not bite. Above that, and on any window replacement in Palos Hills at all, it decides how the room is sealed and how it is left. On 5.3-room housing that threshold arrives early.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Palos Hills.

Ask about it early. It changes the sequence of a job rather than the price of the paint, and a contractor who has thought about it will tell you in plain terms what happens on day one.

This site does not claim EPA lead-safe firm certification. No number has been supplied, so the trust panel below shows it as pending. Ask for it directly, from anyone quoting work in Palos Hills.

Questions

Asked about Palos Hills

Is the $259,200 median home value in Palos Hills what a job here costs?

They are two different things. $259,200 is a published estimate of home value in Palos Hills and nothing more. Cost of work depends on what is on the walls now, how much trim there is and what has to come off before anything goes on, and none of that is knowable from a median.

Who actually shows up in Palos Hills?

Mike Walsh owns the company, walks the job and stays on it while our crew works. Call 708-935-4289. It is worth saying because on a job this size the gap between whoever measured it and whoever turns up is where most of the disappointment comes from.

Can it be done a room at a time?

It can. Splitting a 5.3-room house into phases is normal and it is priced as phases rather than as a discount on the whole. The trade-off is setup time, because masking and protecting a room costs the same whether it is one room or the fourth.

What changes the price most on a house here?

Condition, not size. On 1977-median stock in Palos Hills what varies is how much has to come off or be made good before anything goes on: loose paint, failed caulk, damaged trim, ceilings that have been patched before. Two houses on the same street can differ by a lot on that alone.
